Weigh at least:

- theme: what the image makes perceptible (what passes and what remains, what

- speaker: the same speaker, addressee or stance (a command to glorify, a

  nearer life);
- contrast: the same scene or object carrying the opposite, or a boundary;
- neighbour: the ayat next to a passage you name, when the scene continues
  there.

Before grading candidates, work through every distinct scene, object, action,
relation, and secondary dictionary sense actually developed in the section.
For each, recall direct formulations, repeated occurrences elsewhere,
nonlexical parallels, and relevant reversals. Do not let the title, the first
scene, or the ayat already quoted stand in for the whole section. The same
ayah may qualify for more than one image, for different stated reasons. For
a Buluşmalar section, also consider the particular meetings between images
that its prose develops. Do this review internally; output only the TSV rows.

Search exhaustively for connections specific to this image. Scene, root,
theme, speaker, contrast, and neighbour are ways to discover candidates;
each candidate still needs a concrete connection.

For every included ayah, identify the particular detail or claim in this
section, the corresponding detail in the ayah's own context, and what their
relationship adds to the reader's understanding. Put this connection in
short_explanation, in English, with the Arabic word where a word carries
the link. Keep Arabic quotations short and quote only words you remember as
belonging to the cited ayah. If exact wording is uncertain, explain the
connection in English instead of reconstructing a quotation. Explicitly label
a root, dictionary form, or wording from the source section as such. Never
combine words from different ayat into one quotation; mark omitted words.
Check the speaker, action, negation, and ayah boundary in your remembered
context. If a neighbour is needed to complete the claim, name that ayah and
describe the cited row's own contribution separately.

Shared vocabulary, a broad religious theme, or the same speaker alone is
insufficient. Do not introduce imagery into your explanation that neither
passage supports. Preserve indirect, parallel, secondary, and contrary
readings when you can state their specific connection; do not pick one
preferred meaning. A shared word is not required. The whole surah supplies
context; the selected image defines the scope.

Include every candidate meeting this standard. There is no target list
length. For a neighbour, name the linked ayah and explain what the neighbour
completes; proximity alone does not qualify it or make it strong.

Examples of the inclusion boundary for an image about a guide, the middle
of the way, and losing the way (these are examples, not automatic candidates
for other images):
- Include 2:108: ضَلَّ سَوَاءَ السَّبِيلِ directly connects losing the way

- Do not include 103:1 on the explanation that time measures "the repeated
  ground on which the path is walked": that explanation invents a path
  connection around the oath by time.

strength	ayah_ref	basis	short_explanation

- strong: a direct, specific correspondence to an identifiable feature of this
  image, including a secondary feature actually developed in the prose;
- medium: a specific correspondence whose interpretive bridge you can state
  explicitly;
- weak: a plausible, specific correspondence whose uncertainty you identify

- contrast: a specific reversal or boundary that illuminates the image.

Contrast describes the kind of relationship, not a lower confidence level.
Use it when the principal link is a reversal or boundary; explain any
uncertainty in the note. Whenever an otherwise graded row also makes a
contrast, include contrast among its bases. Neither model agreement nor a
follow-up origin makes a candidate stronger.

Even a weak candidate must meet the inclusion standard. Use only these
bases, joined by + when several hold: scene, root, theme, speaker, contrast,
neighbour. Write the ayah reference as canonical surah:ayah, one ayah per row,
no ranges: consecutive ayat get their own rows. Strongest first.

Do not write a header row, rank numbers, Markdown, sections, commentary or

# Surah 1, image section 12: Gözden kaybolmak: yolcuyu götüren yol ve toprakta yitip giden

## The section's prose (Turkish commentary)

Bir şeyin gözden kaybolmasının iki türü vardır. "Sırat" kelimesinin kökü, geçip giderken gözden kaybolmayı anlatır: {ar:أصل صحيح واحد يدل على غيبة في مر وذهاب؛ سرطت الطعام إذا بلعته لأنه إذا سرط غاب, tr:aslun sahîhun vâhidun yedüllü alâ gaybetin fî merrin ve zehâb; seratu't-taâme izâ bele'tüh, gloss:geçip giderken gözden kaybolmaya işaret eden bir köktür; yemeği yuttuğumda "seratu" derim, çünkü yutulan yemek kaybolur, source:"ص ر ط,B002"}. Yutulan lokma boğazdan geçer ve gider, fakat bedenin içinde varması gereken yere varır. Bir açıklamaya göre yol da bu adı aynı sebeple almıştır: {ar:لأن الذاهب فيه يغيب, tr:li-enne'z-zâhibe fîhi yegîb, gloss:çünkü yolda giden gözden kaybolur, source:"ص ر ط,B001"}. Yolcu yol boyunca ilerler ve bakanın gözünden çıkar, ama yolun bir yönü ve bir varış yeri vardır. Yedinci ayetin son kelimesi ise öbür türü anlatır: {ar:ضل الشيء إذا خفي وغاب؛ أئذا ضللنا في الأرض أي خفينا وغبنا, tr:dalle'ş-şey'ü izâ hafiye ve gâb, gloss:şey gizlenip kayboldu; "toprakta kaybolduğumuzda mı" sözü, gizlenip yok olduğumuzda demektir, source:"ض ل ل,B002"}. Bu kelimenin aslı kaybolmaktır: {ar:أصل الضلال الغيبوبة, tr:aslü'd-dalâli'l-gaybûbe, gloss:dalâlin aslı kaybolmaktır, source:"ض ل ل,B002"}. Ölü toprağa gömüldüğünde bu fiil kullanılır: {ar:أضل الميت إذا دفن, tr:udılle'l-meyyit, gloss:ölü gömüldü, source:"ض ل ل,B002"}. Suya karışan süt de böyle anılır: {ar:ضل اللبن في الماء ثم استهلك, tr:dalle'l-lebenü fi'l-mâ', gloss:süt suya karışıp kayboldu, source:"ض ل ل,B002"}. Kimsenin nereye gittiğini bilmediği kişi için de aynı söz söylenir: {ar:ذهب فلان ضلة إذا لم يدر أين ذهب, tr:zehebe fülânün dılleten, gloss:falanca gitti ve nereye gittiği bilinmedi, source:"ض ل ل,B003"}. Hafızadan silinen bir şey de bu kelimeyle anlatılır: {ar:أن تضل إحداهما أي تغيب عن حفظها أو يغيب حفظها عنها, tr:en tadılle ihdâhümâ, gloss:biri unutursa, yani olay hafızasından kaybolursa, source:"ض ل ل,B004"}.

Bu iki tanım aynı fiili, "gâbe"yi kullanır. Yolcu yolda kaybolur, kaybolan şey de toprakta ya da suda kaybolur. Aradaki fark nereye gidildiğindedir. Altıncı ve yedinci ayetler bu iki kayboluşu karşı karşıya koyar. Sırat, yolcuyu gözden çıkarır, fakat bir yere ulaştırır. Dalâl ise kişiyi nereye gittiği bilinmeyecek şekilde yok eder. Düz bir meal "dosdoğru yol" ile "sapanlar"ı birbirinin zıddı sayar. Görüntü ise ikisinin de bir gidiş olduğunu, birinin varılacak yeri olduğunu, öbürünün olmadığını gösterir.

Kur'an'da bu kayboluş birçok sahnede yer alır. Dirilişi inkâr edenler şöyle sorar: {ar:أَءِذَا ضَلَلْنَا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ أَءِنَّا لَفِى خَلْقٍۢ جَدِيدٍۭ, tr:e-izâ dalelnâ fi'l-ardı e-innâ le-fî halkın cedîd, gloss:toprakta kaybolup gittiğimizde mi yeniden yaratılacağız, source:32:10}. Kur'an bu soruyu şöyle cevaplar: {ar:بَلْ هُم بِلِقَآءِ رَبِّهِمْ كَٰفِرُونَ, tr:bel hüm bi-likâi rabbihim kâfirûn, gloss:hayır, onlar Rablerine kavuşmayı inkâr ediyorlar, source:32:10}. Onlara göre toprakta kaybolmak bir son, Kur'an'a göre ise bir kavuşmanın yoludur. Hepsinin toplanacağı günde şirk koşanlara ortakları sorulur {source:6:22}. Uydurdukları şeyler o zaman kaybolup gider: {ar:وَضَلَّ عَنْهُم مَّا كَانُوا۟ يَفْتَرُونَ, tr:ve dalle anhüm mâ kânû yefterûn, gloss:uydurdukları şeyler onlardan kaybolup gitti, source:6:24}. Din gününde kimse gözden kaybolamaz: {ar:وَمَا هُمْ عَنْهَا بِغَآئِبِينَ, tr:ve mâ hüm anhâ bi-gâibîn, gloss:oradan uzaklaşıp kaybolamazlar, source:82:16}. Firavun Musa'ya geçmiş nesilleri sorar {source:20:51}. Musa şöyle cevap verir: {ar:عِلْمُهَا عِندَ رَبِّى فِى كِتَٰبٍۢ ۖ لَّا يَضِلُّ رَبِّى وَلَا يَنسَى, tr:ilmühâ inde rabbî fî kitâb, lâ yadıllu rabbî ve lâ yensâ, gloss:onların bilgisi Rabbimin katında bir kitaptadır; Rabbim ne bir şeyi kaybeder ne de unutur, source:20:52}. Burada "dalle" fiili, unutmanın yanında, bir şeyin izini yitirmek anlamında kullanılır ve Rabden bu kayıp tamamen uzak tutulur. Yusuf'un kuyudaki kayboluşu ise varış yeri olan bir kayboluştur. Kardeşleri onu {ar:غَيَٰبَتِ ٱلْجُبِّ, tr:gayâbeti'l-cübb, gloss:kuyunun gözden ırak dibi, source:12:10} denilen yere atmak ister, fakat bu kaybolma onu bir yola, yolcuların eline ulaştırır. Gözü kapatılmış kimseler ise yolu bulmak için koşuşur: {ar:فَٱسْتَبَقُوا۟ ٱلصِّرَٰطَ فَأَنَّىٰ يُبْصِرُونَ, tr:festebeku's-sırâta fe-ennâ yübsırûn, gloss:yola doğru koşuşsalar da nasıl görebilirler, source:36:66}.

## The ayat of the surah this image rests on (Arabic)

1:6	ٱهْدِنَا ٱلصِّرَٰطَ ٱلْمُسْتَقِيمَ
1:7	صِرَٰطَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ غَيْرِ ٱلْمَغْضُوبِ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا ٱلضَّآلِّينَ

## Roots and words the section names (ayah, word, root, branch)

1:6	ٱلصِّرَٰطَ	ص ر ط	B001, B002
1:7	صِرَٰطَ	ص ر ط	B002
1:7	ٱلضَّآلِّينَ	ض ل ل	B002, B003, B004

## The whole surah 1 (Arabic)

1:1	بِسْمِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ
1:2	ٱلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
1:3	ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ
1:4	مَٰلِكِ يَوْمِ ٱلدِّينِ
1:5	إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ وَإِيَّاكَ نَسْتَعِينُ
1:6	ٱهْدِنَا ٱلصِّرَٰطَ ٱلْمُسْتَقِيمَ
1:7	صِرَٰطَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ غَيْرِ ٱلْمَغْضُوبِ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا ٱلضَّآلِّينَ

*** Add File: _commentary/v16/out/s001/discovery/revision4/sec12/terra/list.tsv
+strong\t32:10\tscene+root+theme\tThe source's "lost in the earth" is the challengers' \u0636\u064e\u0644\u064e\u0644\u0652\u0646\u064e\u0627 \u0641\u0650\u064a \u0627\u0644\u0652\u0623\u064e\u0631\u0652\u0636\u0650: burial is treated as erasure, while the ayah exposes their denial of meeting their Lord.
+strong\t32:11\tneighbour+theme+contrast\tThe reply to 32:10 gives the supposedly vanished person a fixed course: the angel takes them at death and then they are returned to their Lord.
+strong\t20:52\troot+theme+contrast\tMoses says of the record of past generations that his Lord neither loses track, \u0644\u064e\u0627 \u064a\u064e\u0636\u0650\u0644\u064f\u0651, nor forgets; it directly reverses both source senses of \u0636\u064e\u0644\u064e\u0644 as loss and failed memory.
+strong\t20:53\tscene+neighbour+theme\tImmediately after the Lord who does not lose or forget, He makes paths through the earth; known-making and route-making meet in the same reply.
+strong\t2:282\troot+theme\t\u062a\u064e\u0636\u0650\u0644\u064e\u0651 describes one witness's memory failing so the other can remind her, the source's explicit secondary sense of \u0636\u064e\u0644\u064e\u0644 as something lost from remembrance.
+strong\t6:22\tneighbour+scene+theme\tThe gathering of all the associators supplies the judgment scene in which their claimed partners will prove absent in 6:24; none can disappear from that assembly.
+strong\t6:24\troot+scene+theme\tTheir inventions \u0636\u064e\u0644\u064e\u0651 \u0639\u064e\u0646\u0652\u0647\u064f\u0645\u0652, vanish away from them at judgment, giving the source's loss-image a concrete eschatological scene.
+strong\t6:94\troot+scene+theme\tArriving before God one by one, they find the intercessors they claimed gone from them; the verse makes false attachments disappear while persons still arrive.
+strong\t7:53\troot+scene+theme\tWhen the promised outcome comes, what they invented has vanished from them; the source's contrast between a real destination and loss is enacted at the Day.
+strong\t10:28\tneighbour+scene+theme\tThe Day separates worshippers from their alleged partners, preparing the disappearance of fabricated claims in 10:30 rather than leaving an undifferentiated crowd.
+strong\t10:30\troot+scene+theme\tEach soul is tested by what it sent ahead, then its inventions \u0636\u064e\u0644\u064e\u0651 \u0639\u064e\u0646\u0652\u0647\u064f\u0645\u0652; claims vanish, but the soul returns to its true Lord.
+strong\t11:21\troot+theme\tThose people have lost themselves, and what they used to invent disappears from them; loss here consumes both the traveler and the false route imagined for him.
+strong\t16:86\tneighbour+scene\tSeeing the partners they had associated exposes the alleged guides before 16:87 says their inventions have vanished; the visual encounter makes the later loss specific.
+strong\t16:87\troot+scene+theme\tOn that Day they yield to God and their inventions vanish from them, another explicit judgment form of the source's \u0636\u064e\u0644\u064e\u0651-as-gone-away.
+strong\t17:67\tscene+root+theme\tIn danger at sea, all whom they call upon disappear from them except God; water makes the source's image of something lost in water into a test of the only reliable destination.
+strong\t40:74\troot+scene+theme\tAsked where their partners are, they answer, "\u0636\u064e\u0644\u064f\u0651\u0648\u0627 \u0639\u064e\u0646\u064e\u0651\u0627"; the imagined companions have vanished at the moment of arrival before God.
+strong\t41:48\troot+scene+contrast\tThose formerly invoked vanish from the people, who then know they have no escape; disappearance here is a boundary, not a way out of judgment.
+strong\t82:16\tscene+contrast+theme\t\u0648\u064e\u0645\u064e\u0627 \u0647\u064f\u0645\u0652 \u0639\u064e\u0646\u0652\u0647\u064e\u0627 \u0628\u0650\u063a\u064e\u0627\u0626\u0650\u0628\u0650\u064a\u0646\u064e denies being absent from the Fire, the source's direct counterimage to vanishing from sight.
+strong\t12:10\tscene+theme\tThe brothers propose the \u063a\u064e\u064a\u064e\u0627\u0628\u064e\u0629\u0650 \u0627\u0644\u0652\u062c\u064f\u0628\u0650\u0651, the unseen bottom of a well; the source explicitly reads this disappearance as one that will still carry Joseph onward.
+strong\t12:15\tneighbour+scene+theme\tJoseph is actually put into the well's hidden depth, but the divine message there gives that obscurity a future report and therefore an end.
+strong\t12:19\tneighbour+scene+theme\tThe passing caravan's water-drawer finds Joseph in the well, completing the source's point that this hidden place delivers him into travelers' hands.
+strong\t36:66\tscene+root+theme\tIf their eyes were obliterated, they would race for the \u0635\u0650\u0651\u0631\u064e\u0627\u0637 but be unable to see: the section's blind traveler and road are staged together.
+strong\t6:71\tscene+theme\tThe simile is a person bewildered on the earth after devils have lured him away, while companions call him back to guidance; it is the source's destinationless going versus a called route.
+strong\t6:76\tscene+theme\tAbraham watches a star set and rejects what disappears; the visible vanishing of a supposed lord begins a scene whose next ayah joins guidance and \u0636\u064e\u0644\u064e\u0627\u0644.
+strong\t6:77\tscene+root+theme\tWhen the moon sets, Abraham says that without his Lord's guidance he would be among the \u0636\u064e\u0627\u0644\u0650\u0651\u064a\u0646; disappearing celestial signs and being lost are deliberately adjacent.
+strong\t6:78\tscene+theme\tThe larger sun also disappears, so its setting cannot be the arrival point for Abraham's search; the passage continues the source's contrast between a vanishing object and a true destination.
+strong\t6:79\tneighbour+theme\tAfter the setting lights, Abraham turns his face to the Creator of heavens and earth, giving the preceding failed sightings a directed end.
+strong\t6:59\ttheme+contrast\tLeaves, grain in earth's darkness, and every moist or dry thing remain in a clear record; what is hidden in earth is never lost to the knower who does not \u064a\u064e\u0636\u0650\u0644\u064f\u0651 or forget.
+strong\t10:61\ttheme+contrast\tNot even an atom in earth or heaven is absent from the Lord, and all is in a clear record; this supplies a close Qur'anic counterpart to the source's lost-in-earth claim.
+strong\t34:3\ttheme+contrast\tNothing of an atom's weight in heaven or earth escapes God's knowledge, however small; physical disappearance never makes a creature unaccountable.
+strong\t57:4\tscene+theme\tGod knows what enters the earth and what comes out of it, precisely the movement the source contrasts with a person thought to have vanished into ground.
+strong\t50:4\tscene+theme+contrast\t"We know what the earth diminishes of them" and a preserved record answer the fear in 32:10: the earth's taking of bodies is measured, not an untraceable loss.
+strong\t20:55\tscene+theme\tFrom earth God creates people, returns them to it, and brings them out again; burial has both a source and a specified exit.
+strong\t7:25\tscene+theme\tHuman life, death in the earth, and being brought out of it form a complete movement rather than the final disappearance imagined in the source's quoted objection.
+strong\t71:18\tscene+theme\tGod returns people to the earth and will bring them forth again, explicitly turning return-to-ground into a passage with an emergence.
+strong\t77:25\tscene+theme\tThe earth is made a container, so its enclosing function gives a physical setting for the source's buried and hidden person.
+strong\t77:26\tneighbour+scene\tThe next ayah specifies that the earth's enclosure includes both living and dead, joining the visible and buried conditions the source sets side by side.
+strong\t80:21\tscene+theme\tAfter death God places the human in a grave; the act of being put out of sight is named as one stage of a divine sequence.
+strong\t80:22\tneighbour+theme\tAfter the grave of 80:21, God's will raises the person, making the concealed stage a pause before a known destination.
+strong\t84:3\tscene+theme\tThe earth is spread out in the final upheaval, beginning the reversal of its normal capacity to hold what has disappeared into it.
+strong\t84:4\tneighbour+scene\tIt casts out what is within it, a direct image of hidden contents no longer remaining lost in the earth.
+strong\t84:5\tneighbour+theme\tThe earth obeys its Lord in releasing its contents, so the emergence in 84:4 is purposive rather than accidental.
+strong\t99:2\tscene+theme\tThe earth brings out its burdens; the source's lost-in-earth image meets a scene in which what it held becomes manifest.
+strong\t100:9\tscene+theme\tWhat is in graves is scattered out, turning a place of concealment into disclosure on the Day of reckoning.
+strong\t36:51\tscene+theme\tAt the Trumpet people hurry out from graves toward their Lord; the journey from buried disappearance has a named recipient.
+strong\t54:7\tscene+theme\tThey emerge from graves and rush toward the caller, a crowd no longer unlocated but summoned along a determined course.
+strong\t18:61\tscene+theme\tAt the meeting of the seas, the fish takes its way into the sea; a thing becoming invisible in water is described through a way, echoing the source's water-loss and route imagery.
+strong\t18:63\tscene+theme\tThe servant says he forgot the fish just as it took its way into the sea, combining the source's memory-loss sense with disappearance in water.
+strong\t18:64\tneighbour+scene+theme\tThe lost fish-sign becomes the route they were seeking, and they return by tracing their steps; disappearance here guides travelers to their intended meeting.
+strong\t18:41\tscene+theme\tA garden's water may sink into the ground so that its owner cannot pursue it, a concrete counterpart to something becoming inaccessible in earth.
+strong\t37:142\tscene+theme\tThe fish swallows Jonah, making him disappear into an unseen interior; like the source's swallowed morsel, loss from sight does not settle his ultimate destination.
+strong\t37:143\tneighbour+theme\tHad Jonah not glorified God, he would have remained in the fish until the resurrection; the hidden enclosure is explicitly bounded by an end.
+strong\t37:145\tneighbour+scene\tGod casts Jonah onto an open shore, completing the movement from swallowed invisibility to visible arrival.
+strong\t20:77\tscene+theme\tMoses is told to make a dry path through the sea for the servants, a literal route across water that protects travelers from being overtaken.
+strong\t20:78\tneighbour+scene\tPharaoh follows them with his forces and the sea overwhelms him; the same water marks the boundary between a guided route and engulfing loss.
+strong\t20:79\tneighbour+root+contrast\tThe verse names Pharaoh as one who led his people astray and did not guide them, interpreting the sea scene in the source's terms of destinationless leadership.
+strong\t6:97\tscene+theme\tStars are made so people can find their way through darknesses of land and sea, furnishing visible guidance where the source imagines a traveler gone from sight.
+strong\t16:9\tscene+theme+contrast\tGod takes responsibility for the direction of the way, while another way is crooked; this is the source's distinction between a route with an end and a going that misses it.

+strong\t27:63\tscene+theme\tGod guides through darknesses of land and sea, bringing the source's lost traveler into the very environments where orientation can fail.
+strong\t43:10\tscene+theme\tThe earth is made a cradle and paths are made in it so people may be guided, directly joining ground, route, and intended guidance.
+strong\t71:19\tscene+theme\tGod spreads the earth for people, preparing the spatial setting for movement rather than an undifferentiated place of disappearance.
+strong\t71:20\tneighbour+scene\tIts purpose is that people travel its broad paths, an explicit traveler-and-way scene alongside the earth imagery.

+strong\t7:16\tscene+root+contrast\tIblis vows to sit for people on God's straight \u0635\u0650\u0631\u064e\u0627\u0637, making the source's road a contested course with an ambush that can turn travelers away.
+strong\t7:86\tscene+root+contrast\tThe people are forbidden to sit on every path threatening travelers and seeking crookedness in God's way; the ayah concretely opposes passage and deliberate derailing.
+strong\t6:153\troot+scene+contrast\tGod's one straight path is to be followed, while other ways scatter people from it; the source's contrast between directed going and lost dispersal is stated spatially.
+strong\t10:25\troot+theme\tGod calls to the Abode of Peace and guides whom He wills to a straight path, giving the source's path an explicit destination.
+strong\t15:41\troot+theme\tGod calls the protected line of access a straight \u0635\u0650\u0631\u064e0627\u0637 upon Him, locating the route's security in a divine guarantee.
+strong\t19:43\tspeaker+root+theme\tAbraham asks his father to follow him so he can guide him to an even path; guidance is offered as a personal redirection away from a perilous attachment.
+strong\t28:22\tscene+theme\tLeaving toward Midian, Moses asks that his Lord guide him to the sound way; a traveler actually seeks orientation and a destination.
+strong\t42:52\tspeaker+root+theme\tRevelation is made a light by which the Messenger guides servants to a straight path, joining the source's road to the ability to see it.
+strong\t42:53\tneighbour+root+theme\tThat path is God's, and all matters finally return to Him; the neighbor makes the path's final arrival explicit.
+strong\t46:30\troot+theme\tThe believing jinn say the Book guides to truth and to a straight way, treating revelation as a reliable direction rather than an unmarked departure.
+strong\t67:15\tscene+theme\tPeople are told to walk the earth's slopes, eat its provision, and remember that resurrection is to God; ordinary travel and final return share one directed horizon.
+strong\t84:6\tscene+theme\tEvery human labors onward toward the Lord and will meet Him, an exact thematic answer to the source's question whether a going has a destination.
+strong\t53:42\ttheme\tThe final end is with the Lord; it supplies the destination denied by the idea that burial makes a person simply vanish.
+strong\t76:3\tscene+theme+contrast\tGod shows the human the way, after which gratitude or ingratitude divides the response; the section's road is a disclosed route with a consequential choice.
+strong\t90:10\tscene+theme+contrast\tThe two ways are shown to the human, making direction a choice between courses rather than an unknowable disappearance.
+strong\t20:123\troot+theme+contrast\tWhoever follows divine guidance will neither go astray nor suffer; this directly pairs a route with escape from the destinationless \u0636\u064e\u0644\u064e\u0627\u0644 of the source.
+strong\t20:124\tneighbour+scene\tTurning from the reminder yields a constricted life and resurrection blind, extending the source's blind would-be traveler beyond 36:66.
+strong\t20:125\tneighbour+scene\tThe resurrected person asks why he is raised blind although he once saw, making lost sight a judgment condition rather than just a physical obstacle.
+strong\t20:126\tneighbour+theme+contrast\tBecause he forgot God's signs, he is forgotten that Day; memory loss receives the reciprocal boundary that contrasts with 20:52's unfailing divine memory.
+strong\t17:48\tscene+root+theme\tTheir hostile descriptions leave them \u0636\u064e\u0644\u064f\u0651\u0648\u0627 so they cannot find a way, an explicit form of the source's unlocated and directionless going.
+strong\t17:72\tscene+root+theme\tOne blind in this life is blind in the next and further astray in way; physical non-seeing is made a path condition.

+strong\t30:53\tscene+root+theme\tAgain, blind people cannot be guided away from their error; the wording preserves the relation between blindness and not leaving \u0636\u064e\u0644\u064e\u0627\u0644.
+strong\t43:36\troot+theme\tWhoever turns from the Reminder receives a devil as companion, a false fellow-traveler who will be shown in the next ayah to turn people from the path.

+contrast\t7:146\tscene+root+contrast\tThose who see the way of right guidance do not take it, but take the way of error when they see it; the verse reverses the traveler's choice at the fork.
+contrast\t14:3\tscene+root+contrast\tThey turn others from God's way and seek crookedness in it, preferring the nearer life; this is the source's path deprived of its proper end.
+contrast\t18:53\tscene+theme+contrast\tThe guilty see the Fire, know they will fall into it, and find no escape; unlike the imagined disappearance, judgment fixes an unavoidable arrival.

+contrast\t25:34\tscene+root+contrast\tThose gathered on their faces toward Hell are worst in place and furthest astray in way, giving the source's road a reversed bodily orientation and end.

+contrast\t38:26\troot+theme+contrast\tFollowing desire leads a judge away from God's path, making inner desire a force that diverts a traveler from a known direction.
